clue.text: A hopeless individual!

parts.note: read straight it sounds like someone utterly useless, but it means a person with no hope, one who always expects the worst

explanation.surface: Someone is written off as utterly useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopeless' usually means incompetent; here it means literally without hope, which describes a gloomy outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who always expects the worst outcome is lacking in hope, literally hope-less.

clue.text: Jail an engineer as punishment for wrongdoing

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure, slang for a prison
CE stands for Civil Engineer

explanation.surface: An engineer is locked up as a penalty for a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-punishment or a penalty accepted to atone for a sin.

clue.text: Attendants' anger about break-out

annotationWithheld.why: 'Attendants' anger about break-out' (9): ENTOURAGE; anger + out anagrams to eight letters, one E short, and no other parse found; likely OCR loss, no source found

clue.text: Being very quiet about a man put inside and creating fear

annotationWithheld.why: 'Being very quiet about a man put inside and creating fear' (9): APPREHEND; A+PP+RE+HE+ND fits pieces but 'Being' and 'and creating' give no clean parse; likely OCR damage, no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: Being very quiet about a man put inside and creating fear

clue.text: She is on after almost everyone

indicators.note: after places the words 'is on' following the shortened word
almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A woman takes her turn once nearly everyone else has had theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final letter of the word for everyone; 'after' puts the next two words behind it. 'She' is the whole definition: any woman's name fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Alison is a girl's name, so it can stand for any woman referred to as she.

clue.text: Properly prepare or train a member of society

indicators.note: to prepare something properly is to put it into proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get ready, or be coached, before joining a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Properly prepare' rearranges ORTRAINA. The 'society' is the Rotary Club, an international service organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rotarian belongs to Rotary International, a service club often referred to as a society.

clue.text: A cleric getting in a joint and a variety of fish

indicators.note: getting in means the cleric and the article go inside the joint

parts.note: a hock is the joint in an animal's hind leg, also a cut of meat
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a clergyman's degree

explanation.surface: A churchman goes into a pub-style joint and there's fish on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in' signals the container. 'A variety of fish' reads like a list, but it is one species.
explanation.definitionFit: Haddock is a species of North Atlantic food fish of the cod family.

clue.text: The press needn't be involved!

parts.note: it reads like keeping journalists out of a story, but pressing here means ironing clothes

explanation.surface: A matter is kept out of the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The press' suggests newspapers; it is ironing, which a crease-resistant fabric does not need.
explanation.definitionFit: Crease-resistant fabric needs no ironing, so pressing with a hot iron can be skipped.

clue.text: Immutable as ever

parts.note: something that never changes and lasts for ever, so it describes what is everlasting

explanation.surface: Something remains unchanging, just as it always has.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting and unchanging exists without end or alteration, for ever.

clue.text: A trainee seen by the boss before ten, maybe

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud on a surface

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word ten could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A new recruit is seen by the boss before ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals the anagram of TEN, giving ENT. 'Boss' is not an employer but a raised ornament on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A student is a learner under instruction, someone being trained.

clue.text: Tempers shown — in this case a son seems to blame

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the following words of the clue

explanation.surface: Tempers flare and, in this situation, a son seems to be at fault.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through caSE A SON Seems. 'Tempers' is a verb: to season is to moderate or temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To season is to moderate or soften, just as one tempers justice with mercy.

clue.text: Past directors in deep water

parts.note: over means finished, past
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Former company directors are now in serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In deep water' suggests trouble, but here it is literal: fallen from a ship into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over the side of a ship puts someone in the sea, literally in deep water.

clue.text: House well-liked but unscrupulous person

parts.note: a villa is a large house
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A popular house belongs to a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wicked, dishonest person, a scoundrel.

clue.text: It's pasta for a Roman possibly round about one

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation
possibly says the words a Roman may be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
C is short for circa, about
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Italian perhaps eats pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AROMAN to MAARON; 'round' puts it around C, then I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a tube-shaped pasta.

clue.text: Appealing in regal fashion

definitions.meaning: making a request, putting a question
the phrase '...' means in a royal manner

explanation.surface: A monarch makes a request with royal style.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer reads 'as king', like a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking is requesting; split as two words it means acting like a monarch.

clue.text: Where there's plenty of space for cattle?

definitions.text: Where there's plenty of space for cattle?

parts.words: Where there's plenty of space for cattle?
parts.note: farm animals are livestock, so a room for livestock is jokingly a place to keep goods

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where the herd can graze freely.
explanation.walkthrough: Cattle are 'stock', so a room for them is a joke on the store for goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A storage area for goods, playfully read as space for livestock.

clue.text: Produced information reckoned to be without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the two words surround the point

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
rated means judged, reckoned
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Information thought to be pointless was produced anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking, so the two words surround the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to create or bring into being.

clue.text: Daring to inflame a group of conservationists

parts.note: to gall is to irritate or chafe
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: It takes courage to anger a group of environmentalists.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant person is brave and spirited.

clue.text: As mature as non-professionals can be

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters of 'As mature' could take a new form

explanation.surface: Unpaid players can be as grown-up as the pros.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurs take part for pleasure rather than pay.

clue.text: If Daisy was agreeable she'd be onto this!

definitions.text: If Daisy was agreeable she'd be onto this!

parts.words: If Daisy was agreeable she'd be onto this!
parts.note: the old song 'Daisy Bell' asks Daisy for her answer and promises a bicycle made for two

explanation.surface: A suitor hopes a girl will say yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy Bell' is a popular 1892 song: 'you'll look sweet upon the seat of a bicycle built for two'.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-seater bicycle, as promised to Daisy in the song.

clue.text: Place article in bay say

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
bay is an example of a tree, the bay laurel

explanation.surface: An article is put in a bay, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is a Liverpool racecourse, home of the Grand National. 'Bay' suggests the sea, but it is the laurel.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a town near Liverpool, a locality known for its racecourse.

clue.text: Debtor seeking somebody to draw up a plan

definitions.text: somebody to draw up a plan

parts.note: DR is the accounting abbreviation for debtor or debit
to be after something is to be seeking it

explanation.surface: A person in debt looks for someone to plan a way out.
explanation.definitionFit: One who drafts is a writer of preliminary versions, or a designer of plans.

clue.text: The unit in support set off

indicators.note: in means one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
a unit is one

explanation.surface: The unit, in a supporting role, departs.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer is to start or initiate something new.

clue.text: Write in with directions about plagiarism

indicators.note: about means the directions go around the other word

parts.note: S and E are compass directions, south and east
the second compass direction, east
to crib is to copy someone's work

explanation.surface: Someone writes in with complaints about copying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts S and E around CRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe is to write or engrave words on a surface.

clue.text: Back-issue about furious migrants

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes around the other piece
back means the word for issue is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: issue means offspring, a son
mad means angry

explanation.surface: An old magazine number about angry migrants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns the word for issue around, making NOS; 'about' puts it around the second piece. 'Back-issue' looks like an old magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads are wanderers who move from place to place.

clue.text: Somewhat slow and plodding worker in love

parts.note: the ant is the proverbial hard worker
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A slow, plodding worker is in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a musical tempo marking, slightly faster or slower than andante, a moderate pace.

clue.text: Devastate with an expression of thanks for a pot-plant

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a gift by thanking for a houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: Maranta, the prayer plant, is a tropical genus often grown indoors.

clue.text: Correcting posture, he changed his shape

indicators.note: correcting suggests putting the letters of posture right, so they move

explanation.surface: A man fixed his posture and altered his figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Proteus is the Greek sea god who could change shape at will.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek sea god could change his form at will.

clue.text: See this as episcopal trust

parts.note: a bishop's see is the district in his charge, entrusted to him

explanation.surface: Someone is told to view something as the church's responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but a bishop's see is his district.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's district is his see, entrusted to his care.

clue.text: Such women will certainly succeed

parts.note: it reads as women sure to do well, but succeed here means inherit

explanation.surface: Certain women are destined for success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' means inherit, as an heir succeeds to an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Female inheritors who come into their legacy.
